findings.title: Compilation failure: call to non-existent no-arg `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()`
findings.body: `UsernameForm.authenticate` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but the superclass `UsernamePasswordForm` only defines `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`. No zero-argument overload exists in the class hierarchy, so `UsernameForm` fails to compile. Pass `context.getUser()` (i.e. `!isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`) or match the method signature in `UsernamePasswordForm`.

findings.title: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` returns `false` when `user` is `null`, breaking passkey login on initial authentication
findings.body: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` returns `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`. During a normal initial login (before a user has been identified) or after a failed login where the user is cleared from the context, `context.getUser()` is `null`. Because of the `&& user != null` check, `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` evaluates to `false` in both `authenticate()` (line 115) and `challenge()` (line 137), so `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` is never called and passkey/conditional UI authentication is never initialized on the login page. When `user` is `null`, conditional passkeys must still be enabled if passkeys are enabled for the realm (e.g. `user == null || webauthnAuth.configuredFor(session, session.getContext().getRealm(), user)`).
